title: 👑 Elite Challenge ⭐⭐⭐⭐: Master of the World Map

questions.prompt: A pupil writes about her holidays. Which sentence is correct?

options.text: I met a Indian on the train.
I saw an cape in the shop.
I saw an island from a boat.
I saw a amphitheatre in Rome.

questions.explanation: The word island begins with the vowel i, so it takes an. Indian and amphitheatre begin with a vowel and need an, and cape begins with a consonant and needs a: the choice never comes from the meaning, only from the first letter of the word that follows.

questions.prompt: The unit names five monuments. Which sentence about the pyramids is correct?

options.text: The pyramids are older of the five.
The pyramids are the most old of the five.
The pyramids are the older of the five.
The pyramids are the oldest of the five.

questions.explanation: Five monuments make a whole group, and the first place of a group needs both ends of the tool: the in front and -est behind, so the pyramids are the oldest of the five. The ending -er belongs to two things compared, and a short adjective never takes most in front of it.

options.text: How about travel by plane to Spain?
How about travelling by plane in Spain?
How about travelling by plane to Spain?
Let's travelling by plane to Spain?

questions.explanation: Three rules meet here: after How about the verb takes -ing, the plane is a vehicle so it takes by, and Spain is a place so it takes to. Each of the other sentences breaks exactly one of them, with the bare travel, the preposition in in front of the country, or the -ing form after Let's, which always wants the bare verb.

questions.prompt: Read: "The road from Tunis to Sousse is 140 kilometres long, and the road from Tunis to Gabes is 400 kilometres long." Which sentence is correct?

options.text: The road to Sousse is shorter than the road to Gabes.
The road to Sousse is more short than the road to Gabes.
The road to Sousse is shorter that the road to Gabes.
The road to Sousse is the shortest than the road to Gabes.

questions.explanation: Two roads are compared, and 140 kilometres is less than 400, so the road to Sousse is the shorter one: the short adjective takes -er and the second road follows than. A short adjective never takes more in front of it, a comparison is closed by than and not by that, and the ending -est belongs to a whole group and refuses than.

questions.prompt: Which sentence describes a custom of Spain correctly?

options.text: In Spain, people are eating paella.
In Spain, people ate paella.
In Spain, people eat paella.
In Spain, people will eat paella.

questions.explanation: A custom is what people do again and again, year after year, so it is told in the simple present: In Spain, people eat paella. The form are eating describes this minute only, ate puts the custom in a finished past, and will eat sends it to a day that has not come yet.

questions.prompt: Read: "Karim lives in Tunis. First he travels to Gabes, in the south of the country, and then to Tabarka, in the north-west." In which direction does Karim travel first?

options.text: east
north
north-west
south

questions.explanation: The text says he goes first to Gabes, which is in the south of the country, so his first journey takes him south. The direction north-west is the second one, towards Tabarka, and neither north alone nor east is named anywhere in the text.
